speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset vertigo. To help me determine the cause, can you describe the specific type of spinning sensation you feel and whether it is triggered by head movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

Given the sudden onset of spinning sensations lasting only 3 minutes while changing position (going to bed), accompanied by nausea and vomiting, this presentation is highly characteristic of BPPV. Would you say the dizziness was specifically triggered by turning your head or rolling over in bed?
